statement.summary: Corollary 7.1 is frozen as the conjunction `probUnifCorollaryStatement` of seven Props: `probSandwichStatement` (both real inequalities), `decayIdentityStatement` (P = σ^{−cN}), `decayIntervalStatement` = `decayLowerUniformStatement` (uniform ε–M form of c ≥ 1/2 − o(1)) ∧ `decayUpperStatement` (c ≤ 1 − 1/p₁), `decayLowerExplicitStatement` (c ≥ 1/2 − log_σ K/N), `singleSubgroupStatement`, `probSingleLowerStatement` (P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N}), and `probSingleLowerIsRateLowerStatement` (the parenthetical as a per-instance ↔). P^unif is `probUnif = |S|/σ^{n^d}` in ℝ and c is `decayRate`.

lean_decls.role: statement ('also the lower bound of Prop. 10.1')

deltas: Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 (Definition 2.1) are explicit antecedents of every part; the corollary itself states none.
P^unif is defined as the real number |S_{n^d}|/σ^{n^d} (`probUnif`); the uniform distribution is not modelled as a measure.
F_d(n,σ) is `lowerEnvelope` (q-Pascal binomials at q = n, an integer, cast to ℝ); equal to the paper's product-formula F_d by `envelopeIntegralStatement`.
σ^{−n^d}, σ^{−n^d/2}, σ^{N/p₁−N}, σ^{−cN} are real powers (`Real.rpow`) of σ > 0; log₂ = `Real.logb 2`, log_σ = `Real.logb σ`.
'decays as σ^{−cN}' is the exact identity P = σ^{−cN} (true by the definition of c, given P > 0).
'c ≥ 1/2 − o(1) in any regime with N → ∞' is the uniform statement ∀ε>0 ∃M ∀(n,d,σ) with n^d ≥ M: c ≥ 1/2 − ε (implies every regime; uniform also in σ).
The attribution 'the lower end is Theorem 6.3(ii)' is frozen as its consequence c ≥ 1/2 − log_σ(2^d−1+2 log₂ n)/N.
The single-subgroup Prop adds the count |Fix(C)| = σ^{N/p₁} as a conjunct (implicit in 'which gives').
'(this is also the lower bound of Proposition 10.1)' is read as the per-instance equivalence of P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N} with σ^{N/p₁} ≤ |S_{n^d}|.

maps.label: Corollary 7.1 = conjunction of seven Props

lean.text: probSandwichStatement ∧ decayIdentityStatement ∧ decayIntervalStatement ∧ decayLowerExplicitStatement ∧ singleSubgroupStatement ∧ probSingleLowerStatement ∧ probSingleLowerIsRateLowerStatement

maps.note: The corollary's sentence is split into seven Props: the sandwich; 'decays as σ^{−cN}'; the interval for c (lower and upper ends); the explicit lower end; the single-subgroup inclusion; P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N}; and the parenthetical 'this is also the lower bound of Proposition 10.1'.

maps.label: standing n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: The corollary states no hypotheses. Lean takes the standing ones from Definition 2.1 (σ ≥ 2, as in Theorems 6.1 and 6.3, which both ends rely on) as explicit antecedents of every part.

maps.label: uniform draw from Σ^{n^d} ⇒ P^unif = |S|/σ^{n^d}

tex.text: For a configuration drawn uniformly from $\Sigma^{n^d}$,

maps.note: Lean does not model the uniform distribution as a measure. It takes the paper's own formula P^unif = |S_{n^d}|/σ^{n^d} as the definition. (By contrast, Corollary 7.2 builds an explicit PMF.)

maps.label: P^unif_{n^d} = |S_{n^d}|/σ^{n^d}

lean.text: (numSS n d σ : ℝ) / (σ : ℝ) ^ (n ^ d)
Nat.card {s : Config n d (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s}

maps.note: A real number. The alphabet is `Fin σ`, |S| = `numSS`, and σ^{n^d} is a natural-number power cast to ℝ.

maps.label: F_d σ^{−n^d} ≤ P^unif ≤ (2^d−1+2 log₂ n) σ^{−n^d/2}

lean.text: (lowerEnvelope n d σ : ℝ) * (σ : ℝ) ^ (-((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ probUnif n d σ ∧ probUnif n d σ ≤ closedPrefactor n d * (σ : ℝ) ^ (-(((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2))

maps.note: The chained inequality is a conjunction of two real inequalities.

maps.label: lower: F_d(n,σ) σ^{−n^d} ≤ P^unif

lean.text: (lowerEnvelope n d σ : ℝ) * (σ : ℝ) ^ (-((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ probUnif n d σ

maps.note: Theorem 6.1 divided by σ^{n^d}.

maps.label: F_d(n,σ)

lean.text: (lowerEnvelope n d σ : ℝ)
∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 dd, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (r + 1) * (rdCoeff n r dd : ℤ) * (σ : ℤ) ^ (n ^ (dd - r))
paperEnvelope n d σ = (lowerEnvelope n d σ : ℚ)

maps.note: F_d is the frozen `lowerEnvelope` (an integer, cast ℤ → ℝ). It uses `rdCoeff n r d = n^{C(r,2)}·gaussBinom n d r`. Its identity with the paper's product-formula F_d is the separately proved `envelopeIntegralStatement`.

maps.label: σ^{−n^d}
maps.note: Real power (`Real.rpow`) of σ > 0 with exponent −N.

maps.label: P^unif_{n^d} (in the sandwich)

lean.text: probUnif n d σ

maps.note: `probUnif n d σ`, defined above as |S|/σ^{n^d}.

maps.label: upper: P^unif ≤ (2^d−1+2 log₂ n) σ^{−n^d/2}

lean.text: probUnif n d σ ≤ closedPrefactor n d * (σ : ℝ) ^ (-(((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2))

maps.note: Theorem 6.3(ii) divided by σ^{n^d}.

maps.label: 2^d − 1 + 2 log₂ n

lean.text: closedPrefactor n d
(2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1 + 2 * Real.logb 2 n

maps.note: Same real prefactor as in Theorem 6.3(ii); log₂ = `Real.logb 2`.

maps.label: σ^{−n^d/2}
maps.note: Real power with the real exponent −N/2, which is not an integer for odd N.

maps.label: 'decays as σ^{−cN}' (an exact identity)

lean.text: probUnif n d σ = (σ : ℝ) ^ (-(decayRate n d σ * ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)))

maps.note: Lean reads 'decays as σ^{−cN}' as the exact identity P = σ^{−cN} for the c defined next. Given that definition this is a tautology, apart from P > 0, which is proved (`probUnif_pos`). The substance is the interval for c.

maps.label: N = n^d
maps.note: N is written out as n^d, cast to ℝ.

maps.label: c = log_σ(1/P^unif)/N

lean.text: Real.logb σ (1 / probUnif n d σ) / ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)

maps.note: `decayRate n d σ`; log_σ = `Real.logb σ`. Since P > 0 is proved, the junk values of `1/0` and of the log of a non-positive number never occur.

maps.label: c ∈ [1/2 − o(1), 1 − 1/p₁]

lean.text: decayLowerUniformStatement ∧ decayUpperStatement

maps.note: Interval membership = lower end ∧ upper end.

maps.label: lower end 1/2 − o(1): uniform ε–M form

tex.text: Here $o(1)$ refers to any regime with $N=n^d\to\infty$.

lean.text: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ n d σ : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 1 ≤ d → 2 ≤ σ → M ≤ n ^ d → 1 / 2 - ε ≤ decayRate n d σ

maps.note: ∀ε > 0 ∃M: c ≥ 1/2 − ε for ALL (n, d, σ) with N = n^d ≥ M. This is uniform in n, d and σ jointly, so it implies the limit along every regime with N → ∞, as the paper says. It is at least as strong as the paper's wording, in particular uniform in σ.

maps.label: regime N = n^d → ∞

lean.text: M ≤ n ^ d

maps.note: 'N → ∞' is the guard N ≥ M with M depending only on ε.

maps.label: upper end c ≤ 1 − 1/p₁

lean.text: decayRate n d σ ≤ 1 - 1 / (n.minFac : ℝ)

maps.note: Exact, with no error term, in ℝ.

maps.label: p₁ = smallest prime factor of n

tex.text: where $p_1$ is the smallest prime factor of $n$

lean.text: n.minFac

maps.note: `Nat.minFac n` is the least prime factor for n ≥ 2.

maps.label: 'The lower end is given by Theorem 6.3(ii)'

tex.text: The lower end is given by Theorem~\ref{thm:upper-bound}(ii)

lean.text: 1 / 2 - Real.logb σ (closedPrefactor n d) / ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ decayRate n d σ

maps.note: The attribution is a claim about the proof. Lean freezes its mathematical content, c ≥ 1/2 − log_σ(2^d−1+2 log₂ n)/N (what Theorem 6.3(ii) gives after taking log_σ), and its certificate indeed uses `upperClosed_proved`. The subtracted term is the o(1).

maps.label: Fix(C) ⊆ S_{n^d} for one order-p₁ cyclic C

tex.text: the single-subgroup inclusion $\Fix(C)\subseteq S_{n^d}$ for one order-$p_1$ cyclic subgroup $C$

lean.text: ∃ C : AddSubgroup (Lat n d), IsAddCyclic C ∧ Nat.card C = n.minFac ∧ fixedBy (Fin σ) C ⊆ {s | IsShiftSymmetric s} ∧ Nat.card (fixedBy (Fin σ) C) = σ ^ (n ^ d / n.minFac)

maps.note: An existential: there is a subgroup C that is cyclic, of order p₁, and satisfies Fix(C) ⊆ S, together with the count.

maps.label: one order-p₁ cyclic subgroup C

lean.text: IsAddCyclic C
Nat.card C = n.minFac

maps.note: 'Cyclic' is `IsAddCyclic C` (redundant for prime order, kept to be literal); the order is `Nat.card C`.

maps.label: Fix(C) ⊆ S_{n^d}

lean.text: fixedBy (Fin σ) C ⊆ {s | IsShiftSymmetric s}
{s | ∀ h ∈ H, shift h s = s}

maps.note: Fix(C) = `fixedBy`, and S_{n^d} = the set of `IsShiftSymmetric` configurations.

maps.label: |Fix(C)| = σ^{N/p₁} (implicit in 'which gives')

lean.text: Nat.card (fixedBy (Fin σ) C) = σ ^ (n ^ d / n.minFac)

maps.note: The paper uses this count (Lemma 3.1(i)) silently to go from the inclusion to the probability bound. Lean freezes it as an extra conjunct, with exact ℕ-division (p₁ | n | n^d).

maps.label: P^unif ≥ σ^{N/p₁ − N}

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n.minFac : ℝ) - ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ probUnif n d σ

maps.note: Real inequality.

maps.label: σ^{N/p₁ − N}

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n.minFac : ℝ) - ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ))

maps.note: Real power whose exponent N/p₁ − N is computed in ℝ (an integer, since p₁ | N).

maps.label: '(this is also the lower bound of Proposition 10.1)'

tex.text: this is also the lower bound of Proposition~\ref{prop:rate}

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / (n.minFac : ℝ) - ((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ probUnif n d σ ↔ σ ^ (n ^ d / n.minFac) ≤ numSS n d σ

maps.note: 'Is also' is read as: for each (n, d, σ), P ≥ σ^{N/p₁−N} holds iff σ^{N/p₁} ≤ |S_{n^d}| (the body of Proposition 10.1's lower bound, restated in ℕ). This is a reading choice; the other reading (the same argument proves Prop. 10.1's lower bound) is a claim about proofs and is not frozen.
